thread:
sam: Quick follow-up from the postmortem — extracting the action items we agreed on last night for the KV-cache OOMs. I split into profiling, limits, GC/compaction, dashboards, and rollout. Please ack and take ownership where needed.

sam: Actions I have so far:
- Profiling: capture long-running heap profiles from a reproducer and prod canary (owner: OPEN)
- Soft limits + guards: implement per-shard soft limit and global backpressure path (owner: OPEN)
- GC/compaction: investigate slab compaction heuristics and fragmentation thresholds (owner: OPEN)
- Instrumentation: add per-request residency histograms and allocation tags (owner: OPEN)
- Dashboards & alerts: add a P50/P95 residency and fragmentation alert, plus OOM SLO burn rate (owner: OPEN)

sam: Target is to have owners assigned by EOD and a 2-week remediation plan for the critical items. cc @eng-sre :eyes:

mike: I can take profiling. Will get a reproducible workload and capture 60s heap/alloc traces from canary and prod.
mike: Quick command I'll run on the canary image:```/opt/tools/heapprof --duration=60 --out /tmp/kv-heap-$(date +%s).pb```

mike: Plan to upload traces to the shared bucket + link them in the postmortem doc. ETA: Tue 2026-04-07 EOD. :thumbsup:

jordan: I'll own GC/compaction tuning. Initial plan:
- spike on compaction frequency + aggressive free-list merging
- test flags: `--slab-compaction=aggressive --slab-merge-threshold=0.15`
- run 24h canary with 3x read-heavy load to surface fragmentation regressions

jordan: ETA for first test results: Fri 2026-04-03. Will post perf traces and mem-profiles.

liz: I'll handle dashboards/alerts. Adding these panels: residency histogram, fragmentation ratio, per-shard allocations, OOM count.
liz: PromQL snippets I'll add to the dashboard:```sum by (shard)(kv_resident_bytes) / sum by (shard)(kv_total_bytes)``` and alert when `fragmentation_ratio > 0.30 for 10m`

liz: Also setting an automated Slack alert to #eng-runtime and pager to oncall if OOM count spikes >3 in 10m. ETA: Wed 2026-04-01.

aisa: For rollout: do we want the canary on a Dedicated pool or a small hostpool in hosted? Recommended we use Dedicated to avoid noisy neighbors. I can schedule the canary if we decide.
aisa: also proposing a short blast test (10min ramp) before enabling compaction flags cluster-wide.

deploy-bot: Canary job scheduled: canary-kv-slab-2026-04-01T09:00Z -> cluster:d-004 (owner: aisa)

sam: Thanks — owners now: profiling=mike, gc=jordan, dashboards=liz, canary rollout=aisa. I'll pick up soft limits + instrumentation unless someone volunteers.
sam: Soft limits plan (quick sketch): per-shard soft cap set at 85% of observed steady-state, with background eviction policy that prefers least-recently-used shards; fall back to global backpressure when aggregate resident > 90%.
sam: I'll open a PR for the soft-limit guard rails and a config toggle so we can enable in canary first. ETA: Mon 2026-03-30.

mike: acked. I'll drop links to heap traces in that PR and attach repro steps.
jordan: ack, will coordinate with sam on the canary flags so we don't overlap unsafe changes.
liz: ack, I'll also add a dashboard row for the new soft-limit metric once PR exports it.
aisa: ack — scheduling canary for Apr 1st, but can move earlier if testing is ready.

sam: Cool. Next steps: I'll update the postmortem doc with owners, ETAs, and a small test plan matrix. If anyone needs to reassign, say so in thread. Closing note: prioritize low-risk mitigations (soft limits, alerts) first before aggressive compaction.
sam: Thanks everyone — will follow up with the PR links and a short checklist. :white_check_mark:
